claims.claim: Claude (Mythos Preview and Opus 4.8) autonomously designed protein binders against 16 targets, with binders confirmed for 14 of the 15 targets with interpretable data.
354 of 1,320 designs bound their targets, a hit rate of 26.8% by the integrated call.
Per-target hit rates ranged from 0% (MBP, 0/90) to 80% (TREM2, 72/90), i.e. extreme dispersion around the pooled 26.8%.
The 26.8% figure is an orchestration result: Claude assembled pipelines from ten open-source structure-generation methods (including RFdiffusion and RFdiffusion3), not a single-model design.

RFdiffusion (Watson et al., Nature 2023) reported an overall experimental binder success rate of 19%, across five targets testing fewer than 100 designs each, roughly two orders of magnitude above prior Rosetta-based methods.
Anthropic's blog post does not cite RFdiffusion's 19% as its baseline; it compares against a '10-15% typical' figure from ProteinBase and against Adaptyv's open competitions.
A direct 26.8% versus 19% comparison is not a controlled benchmark because targets, CRO/assay methodology, design budgets and the era of the underlying generators differ.
Mythos Preview hit 26.7% (104/390) and Opus 4.8 hit 22.6% (88/390) in multi-target mode; Mythos Preview hit 35.1% (158/450) in single-target mode; the top-ranked design bound 49% of the time.
On RBX1, 28 of 90 Claude designs bound versus 9 of 245 in the open competition (3.7%), and the tightest reached 3.9 nM against the competition winner's 45 nM re-measured on the same plate.
Claude designed 12 TNFalpha binders (12/150, 8%), all from Opus 4.8, on a target where AlphaProteo and other de novo efforts reported none.
On the novel targets 15-PGDH and latent GDF-8, Claude scored 1/30 and 14/60 respectively, comparable to or better than Adaptyv competition fields (1/106 and 6/100).
The integrated-call binder definition broadened the count above Adaptyv Bio's own classification (roughly 336 of 1,296), adding 19 binders.
The report explicitly disclaims that Claude's designs are better than an expert would obtain with the same tools and budget, and describes 'campaigns rather than models'.
ProteinBase and the Overath et al. corpus consist of roughly 770 binders out of 5,700 designs against 40 targets; Overath et al. analyzed 3,766 characterized binders across 15 targets.
Every model Claude used was open-source; Anthropic releases prompts, models and both CROs' binding data under CC BY 4.0.
